# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-30 (Extended v203)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to summer Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer, Quai des Ormes, Grève, Place du Châtelet, Pont Notre-Dame, Quai de la Mégisserie. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Jondrette's garret, Montfermeil.

Paris sewer system: 5,300 fathoms in 1663; 40,300 metres by 1 January 1832; follows street layout (2,200 streets); ridge divides waters to Seine or Grand Sewer; Sainte-Avoye sewer marks watershed culmination. Grand Sewer (old brook of Ménilmontant) terminates blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant knoll. **Fontis phenomenon** (dangerous water-saturated ground): Depth varies 3-4 to 8-10+ feet; discard loads to escape; death slow if earth predominates, prompt if water predominates. **Champs-Élysées quagmire**: Common obstacle; 1836 Faubourg Saint-Honoré sewer reconstruction took six months due to quicksand. **Sewer outlet design flaw**: Pointed arch vault narrows funnel-like, lower than main gallery—faulty penitentiary-inspired wicket design (later corrected). Heavy grating at river outlet, double-locked with rust-caked lock, rarely swung hinges, iron staple sunk deep. Key exists (held by Thénardier). Beyond: open air, daylight, shore (Grand-Caillou—solitary point), distant quays, bridge of Jéna (downstream), bridge of Invalides (upstream).

**Seine rapid at Châtelet**: Between Pont Notre-Dame and Pont au Change, and Quai de la Mégisserie and Quai aux Fleurs, Seine forms square lake traversed by rapid. Dangerous; hemmed in and irritated by mill piles (now demolished). Two close bridges augment peril; water hurries formidably through arches in vast terrible waves; attacks bridge piles with liquid ropes. Men falling in never reappear.

**Summer Year 8 seasonal conditions**: Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Light went early. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Recent rains swollen river. Darkness complete after midnight; ceiling of clouds concealed stars. Not a single light burned in houses; no one passing; all streets and quays deserted. Notre-Dame and towers of Court-House seemed features of night. Street lantern reddened margin of quay. Bridges lay shapeless in mist. **Wind came off water with salt and tar smell.** Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided same blood debt claim. In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7). **Movie Prydenridge rumored Rorald Lindmere dead of plague; had it from peddler.**

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set on purpose. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate lodgings. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work, moved there (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate lodgings (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there thereafter. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7). Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor wed at Ostcombe, with half the parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. **Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely. In letter Gadrek burned after reading, revealed old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair roof of chapel at Kelmere, and shook on it.**

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. **Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8).**

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Marius's medical condition**: Trunk had no internal injury; bullet deadened by pocket-book, turned aside, made tour of ribs with hideous laceration, not dangerous. Long underground journey dislocated broken collar-bone seriously. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Head fairly covered with cuts; result of head wounds uncertain—might cause brain damage. Grave symptom: swoons caused by wounds; people do not always recover. Wounded man exhausted by hemorrhage. From waist down, barricade protected lower part from injury.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Barricade, Sewer Escape, and Emergence (Chapters 24-29)

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman and officer, smashed helmet. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting, caring. Held peace, lent succor. Received few scratches only.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: Discovered iron grating beneath loose paving-stones leading to dark aperture. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted inert Marius onto shoulders, descended into well three metres below surface, dropped grating behind.

**Sewer journey (6th June, after barricade)**: Escaped via Paris sewer system. **Water flow changed direction**: Gradually perceived water beating against heels instead of toes. Sewer began descending toward belt sewer, not Seine. Ridge forms watershed; Valjean reached culminating point, directed course toward belt sewer. Every encounter with branch felt its angles; avoided narrower ways terminating in blind alleys. **Police patrol (6th June)**: Prefect Gisquet ordered battue of sewers. Three squads explored subterranean drain. Valjean perceived entrance to narrower gallery, passed on. Patrol heard footsteps, raised lantern. Valjean hugged wall, halted. Patrol concluded mistaken, no noise, ought hasten toward Saint-Merry. Before departure, sergeant discharged gun in direction of Valjean; ball struck arch over his head.

**Fontis encounter**: Caused by downpour preceding day. Pavement vanished, entered slime. At supreme moment, struck fragment of vaulting—partly submerged but solid, curved inclined plane. Mounted incline, reached other side. Although exhausted, energy persisted. Reached outlet, raised eyes, perceived light—daylight.

**Outlet entrapment**: Laid Marius down along wall on dry portion. Went to grating, clenched fists, gave frenzied shock—did not move. No lever; no prying possible. Obstacle invincible. Beyond grating: open air, river, daylight, shore, distant quays, Paris, gulf, broad horizon, liberty. Bridges of Jéna (downstream) and Invalides (upstream) discernible. Most solitary point in Paris. Both caught in immense, gloomy web of death.

**Thénardier's appearance and actions**: Thénardier emerged from darkness. Recognized Valjean immediately despite disfigurement. Advised river disposal. Found thirty francs in Marius' coat; tore off strip, concealed under blouse to identify assassin and victim later. Helped Valjean replace Marius on shoulders. **Thénardier's stratagem**: Grating opened to Valjean was Thénardier's cleverness. Thénardier intuitively felt Javert still there—scent never deceiving. Necessary to fling bone to sleuth-hound. By putting Valjean outside, provided prey for police, forced them to relinquish his scent, made them forget him in bigger adventure, repaid Javert for his waiting, earned thirty francs, counted on escaping with aid of diversion.

**Valjean's emergence**: Miasmas, darkness, horror lay behind. Pure, healthful, living, joyous air inundated him. Silence reigned, charming silence of sunset in unclouded azure sky. For several seconds, Valjean irresistibly overcome by august and caressing serenity. Then bent down swiftly to Marius as though sentiment of duty returned. Dipping water in hollow of hand, gently sprinkled few drops on latter's face. Marius' eyelids did not open; half-open mouth still breathed.

**Javert's pursuit and carriage journey (evening 6th June)**: After barricade escape, betook himself to prefecture of police, rendered verbal account to Prefect. Caught sight of Thénardier and followed him. Kept eyes riveted on Valjean. Released Valjean, straightened stiffly up. Glacial silence reigned in carriage. Marius motionless, body resting in corner, head drooping on breast, arms hanging, legs stiff, seemed awaiting only coffin. Valjean seemed made of shadow, Javert of stone. Vehicle full of night.

**Entry and medical care**: Javert first to alight, made sure with one glance of number on carriage gate. Valjean wanted to warn Cosette, tell her where Marius was, give useful information. Valjean pushed open door, entered house, called to porter: "It is I!" and ascended stairs. Marius carried up to first floor, deposited on old sofa in M. Gillenormand's antechamber. Basque went in search of physician. Nicolette opened linen-presses. Jean Valjean felt Javert touch him on shoulder. He understood and descended stairs, having behind him step of Javert following him. **Coachman represented to "monsieur l'Inspecteur" that Utrecht velvet carriage all spotted with blood and mire; added indemnity due; drew certificate book, begged inspector write attestation.**

**M. Gillenormand's emotional crisis (Chapter 29)**: Revolt had deeply agitated, enraged and engrossed mind for past two days. Had not slept on previous night, been in fever all day. Stood astonied on threshold, one hand on handle of half-open door, head bent little forward and quivering, body wrapped in white dressing-gown. Spoke in murmured words of Marius—that he knew Marius was waiting, had arranged his room, placed portrait from childhood, that Marius needed only return and say "It is I" to be master of the house, to be obeyed.

## Javert's Moral Crisis (Chapter 30, Summer Year 8)

**Change in consciousness**: Up to day of Valjean's emergence, Javert borrowed from Napoleon only resolution and certainty. Now, change had taken place; whole person slow and sombre stamped with anxiety. For several hours, Javert ceased to be simple. He was troubled; brain so limpid in its blindness had lost transparency; crystal was clouded. Duty divided within his conscience.

**Encounter at Seine**: When unexpectedly encountered Jean Valjean on banks of Seine, something of wolf regaining grip on prey, and dog finding master again. Beheld two paths, both equally straight, both contrary to each other. Which was true?

**Valjean's transformation in perception**: Jean Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms which supported him all his life crumbled. Valjean's generosity towards Javert crushed him. Facts formerly treated as lies now recurred as realities. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean, two figures superposed, forming one venerable image. Felt something terrible penetrating soul—admiration for convict. Respect for galley-slave—possible thing? Shuddered, could not escape. In inmost heart, confess sublimity of that wretch. Odious.

Benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement, convict returning good for evil, giving pardon for hatred, preferring pity to vengeance, preferring to ruin himself rather than ruin enemy, saving him who smitten him, kneeling on heights of virtue, more nearly akin to angel than man. Javert constrained to admit monster existed.

**Loss of certainty**: Supreme anguish was loss of certainty. Felt uprooted. Code no longer anything but stump in hand. Had to deal with scruples of unknown species. Sentimental revelation entirely distinct from legal affirmation, his only standard hitherto. To remain in former uprightness did not suffice. Whole order of unexpected facts cropped up, subjugated him. Whole new world dawning on soul: kindness accepted and repaid, devotion, mercy, indulgence, violences by pity on austerity, respect for persons, no more definitive condemnation, no more conviction, possibility of tear in eye of law, no one knows what justice according to God, running inverse to justice according to men. Perceived amid shadows terrible rising of unknown moral sun; horrified and dazzled him. Owl forced to gaze of eagle.

**Superior authority consciousness**: This new chief, God, became unexpectedly conscious of; felt embarrassed by him. Unforeseen presence threw off bearings; did not know what to do with superior. **Rift in authority**: Up to this point, everything above merely smooth, limpid, simple surface; nothing incomprehensible, nothing obscure. Authority was plane surface; no fall in it, no dizziness. Never beheld unknown except from below. Now threw self back, suddenly terrified by unprecedented apparition: gulf on high. **Could not return Valjean to Rue de l'Homme Armé. It was clear that was what ought to do. Could not.**

**Javert's final moments (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Traversed Place du Châtelet diagonally, regained quay, returned with automatic precision to very point abandoned quarter hour previously, leaned on elbows, found himself again in same attitude on same paving-stone of parapet. Did not appear to have stirred. Darkness complete, sepulchral moment following midnight. Ceiling of clouds concealed stars. Not single light burned in houses; no one passing; all streets and quays deserted. Street lantern reddened margin of quay. Outlines of bridges lay shapeless in mist. **River could not be seen; only foam audible. At moments, in dizzy depth, gleam of light appeared, undulated vaguely. Wall of quay abrupt, confused, mingled with vapors, instantly concealed, produced effect of escarpment of infinite. Nothing visible but hostile chill of water and stale odor of wet stones felt. Fierce breath rose from abyss. Flood divined rather than perceived, tragic whispering of waves, melancholy vastness of arches of bridge, imaginable fall into gloomy void—all shadow full of horror.**

Remained motionless several minutes, gazing at opening of shadow, considered invisible with fixity resembling attention. Water roared. All at once took off hat, placed it on edge of quay. A moment later, tall black figure appeared erect upon parapet, bent over towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down into shadows; dull splash followed; shadow alone in secret of convulsions of obscure form disappeared beneath water. **Javert is dead (suicide).**

**Police regulation writing (Chapter 30)**: Javert seated at table of post in station-house, mentioned his name, showed card to sergeant. Pen, leaden inkstand and paper provided for possible reports and orders of night patrols. Composed regulation: "Thirdly: mode of keeping track of man with relays of police agents from distance to distance is good, but on important occasions, requisite that at least two agents should never lose sight of each other, so that if one agent should, for any cause, grow weak in his service, other may supervise him and take his place."

**Boulatruelle (Chapter 30)**: For instant was prudent. Escaped neatly from Jondrette's garret in company with other ruffians; his drunkenness had been salvation. Authorities never made out whether he was robber or man robbed. Order of nolle prosequi, founded on authenticated state of intoxication on evening of ambush, set him at liberty. Returned to road from Gagny to Lagny, making broken stone under administrative supervision, downcast mien, pensive mood, ardor for theft somewhat cooled; but addicted nonetheless tenderly to wine which saved him. One morning, before daybreak, caught sight through branches of trees of man, whose back alone he saw, shape of shoulders not entirely unfamiliar. Man did not belong in countryside. Just arrived there. On foot, evidently. No public conveyance passes through Montfermeil at that hour. Had walked all night. Not from great distance; had neither haversack nor bundle. From Paris, no doubt.
